title: Marketplace bundle UX + legal checklist (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc consolidating UX copy variants, SKU/bundle mapping guidance, and legal/compliance flags for cloud marketplace listings (AWS, GCP, Azure). Goal: produce a single checklist and short/long copy set we can hand to partner ops and the listing engineers.

Audience:
- Marketplace program manager (primary)
- Partner ops & legal (review)
- Product marketing (approve final copy)
- Listing engineers / portal devs (implementation)

Current status / context (WIP):
- High-level bundle strategy approved in MP sync (2025-01). Need to finalize: SKU naming convention, free trial entitlements, and marketplace-specific legal callouts.
- Primary launch targets: AWS Marketplace (SaaS), Google Cloud Marketplace (SaaS), Azure Marketplace (VM/Managed Offer as follow-on).
- Dependencies: billing SKU mapping (Billing team), PII & data residency blurb (Security), logos and architecture diagrams (Design).

Quick decisions pending (priority order):
1) Trial model per marketplace: AWS offers 30-day trial vs GCP 14-day — decide universal consumer-facing text vs marketplace-specific text.
2) Billing SKU names: adopt short SKU_id vs human-readable slug. Need billing to confirm format.
3) Legal attribution: where to insert our Data Processing Addendum (DPA) link in listing vs redirect to Redwood website.

Copy variants (short / long) - use as source of truth for portal fields:
- Short headline (1 line / 60 chars recommended):
  * "Redwood Inference — production LLM inference, low-latency, multi-region"
  * alt: "High-throughput LLM inference with predictable SLAs"

- Short description (1–2 sentences):
  * Variant A: "Run production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Transparent pricing, SLA-backed capacity, and model optimization for latency and cost."
  * Variant B (developer-focused): "Ship LLM features quickly with consistent performance across environments. SDKs, observability, and cost controls built for engineering teams."

- Long description / body (for marketplace detail page):
  * Draft: "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime and orchestration layer for serving large language models at production scale. Choose hosted API for rapid integration, reserved Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, or a Private deployment for regulated workloads. Features include streaming responses, intelligent batching and caching, model rollouts, and per-route cost/latency analytics. Integrations: KMS, enterprise SSO, and audit logs. See pricing and SLA details in the plan selector."
  * Callouts to add as bullets: SLA-backed uptime, Reserved capacity options, On-prem/VPC private deployments, SDKs & sample apps, Free trial & onboarding credits.

Marketplace-specific UX notes:
- AWS SaaS: short headline length strict, ensure first 120 chars of long description contains exact value props and trial terms. Add explicit "Starts free: 30-day trial" line if trial is enabled.
- GCP: highlight Marketplace entitlements — must include a Pricing Plan table in the listing. Avoid external links in above-the-fold summary (GCP rejects in some fields).
- Azure: Marketplace often requires co-sell / offerability checks. Prepare a lightweight VM/Managed Offer description that maps to our Dedicated offering for later.

SKU & bundling guidance (draft):
- Strategy: 3 visible offerings per cloud (Simple naming):
  1) Free Trial (time-limited, usage capped)
  2) Pro / Hosted API (pay-as-you-go token pricing + optional reserved seat)
  3) Dedicated / Enterprise (monthly commit with SLA)
- SKU format (proposal): RDW-MP-<cloud>-<tier>-<year> e.g. RDW-MP-AWS-PRO-2025 (billing team to sign off).
- Bundles should map 1:1 to internal product SKUs to avoid reconciliation errors. Inventory table (to align with Billing): SKU, Marketplace offer id, internal product id, price USD, trial_enabled (Y/N).

Mandatory assets checklist (for initial submission):
- Short & long descriptions (approved)
- 1 x hero 1200x600 image (PNG) + 1 x logo (600x60)
- Architecture diagram (PNG) with caption: "Redwood Inference — hosted / dedicated / private"
- Pricing sheet (CSV) mapping SKUs to tiers and list prices
- Contact / support email, onboarding URL, and security whitepaper PDF
- DPA and SOC2 summary: either uploaded or linked per marketplace policy
- Test account credentials and smoke-test script for partner review (expires in 90d)

Legal / compliance flags (items to surface to Legal):
- Data residency claims: do not claim "data never leaves X region" unless Private deployment only. For Hosted / Dedicated, use: "region-aware data controls; see Private deployment for full data residency guarantees."
- Acceptable use policy: include short summary + link. Marketplaces often require an AUP checkbox.
- Trial entitlements & bill-on-conversion: ensure trial billing behavior documented (auto-charge vs manual opt-in) — if auto-charge, need checkout consent language.
- Export controls & model provenance: list any restricted models or countries (legal needs to review).

Acceptance criteria for listing submission (pre-check):
- All copy signed off by PMM and Legal
- Billing SKUs mapped and visible in portal export
- Trial behavior documented and QA’d (test account shows trial limits)
- Security artifacts uploaded (SOC2 summary at minimum)
- Listing assets meet image size & content rules for each marketplace
- UX flow tested end-to-end by Portal QA (submit → provisioning → billing entitlements)

Implementation notes for portal engineers (short):
- Provide a metadata JSON generator that includes: title, short_description, long_description, images[], sku_mapping[], trial_config, legal_blurb_ids[]. Aim to reuse the same generator for AWS/GCP but support per-market overrides.
- Field length constraints: include a validator to warn if long_description exceeds 6k chars or if headline >140 chars.
- Feature flag to turn trial on/off per marketplace during soft launch.

Launch timeline (draft):
- Week 1: finalize copy & SKU mapping (this doc to PMM + Billing)
- Week 2: legal and security reviews complete; portal metadata skeleton implemented
- Week 3: QA + partner review; submit AWS listing + request 30-day trial activation
- Week 4–6: monitor telemetry, fix listing bugs, prepare GCP submission

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Confirm final SKU naming convention with Billing (Owner: Noah)
- [ ] Decide universal trial text vs per-marketplace variants (Owner: Priya)
- [ ] Legal to provide DPA snippet and export-control list (Owner: Evan)
- [ ] Design to deliver hero + architecture PNGs (Owner: Maya)

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratch):
- Consider a "Prepaid committed throughput" SKU for Dedicated that bundles 50M tokens/month at lower unit price — good for channel partners.
- Could offer a "Bring-your-own-model" add-on for Private customers (charges as addon SKU).
- Keep copy modular so we can A/B test headline and trial wording on AWS.

Appendix: example short copy variants to iterate in A/B tests:
1) "Predictable inference at scale — low latency, cost controls, SLA-backed."
2) "Host and serve LLMs with confidence: dedicated pools, auto-bursting, and observability."
3) "Ship features faster with a runtime optimized for production LLMs."

Contact / owners:
- Doc owner: Priya Shah (priya@redwood.com)
- Billing lead: Noah Green (noah@redwood.com)
- Legal reviewer: Evan Torres (evan@redwood.com)
- Design: Maya Li (maya@redwood.com)

End of WIP doc. Update as approvals come in and move to final checklist when items above are resolved.
